author: Irui Wang, MediaTek
subject: PATCH v6 2/6 media: mediatek: encoder: Add a new encoder driver interface
fact: The new interface places source and bitstream addresses in shared firmware parameters and delegates SPS, PPS and frame commands to vpu_enc_encode. It reads the encoded-byte count at0x98 after the IRQ wait.
inference: This examined modern public interface supplies no direct MT6797 source/reference/reconstruction/scratch/start/stop register contract. It cannot justify a firmware-free Gemini encoder backend.

mt6797_owner_review_2026_10_11.scope: Public author-posted GPL patches, pinned Linux codec source, pinned MT6797 GPL wrapper/headers and existing resource/idle evidence only. No canonical mutation, build or hardware action.
mt6797_owner_review_2026_10_11.finding: None of these examined sources provides a firmware-free H264 frame implementation or a complete encoder-register contract demonstrably applicable to MT6797. V4L2 stateful encoder plumbing is reusable, but adding a compatible string or exposing a video node cannot replace the missing frame/DMA backend.

source_proof.fact: Working-buffer sizes and preallocated RC_CODE/SKIP_FRAME addresses come from firmware. SPS/PPS/frame operations call vpu_enc_encode; 0x98 is read after completion, not a frame-programming table.
Input-plane DMA addresses and bitstream DMA address/size are IPI message fields. Their 16-byte alignment and 32/34-bit message layouts are a firmware ABI, not an MT6797 hardware-register contract.
Probe requires mediatek,vpu or mediatek,scp and returns ENODEV without either. Match table lists MT8173/MT8183/MT8188/MT8192/MT8195, not MT6797.

Exact MT6797 GPL source establishes IRQ status/ACK, SPS/PPS/frame/error-related status masks and pause/reset ownership. Encoder MMIO writes in this wrapper are ACK/pause/reset only; no source/reconstruction/scratch/bitstream/start programming is supplied.
GPL HAL init/deinit return success; command-queue/power/ISR cases are empty. This does not supply an encoder frame backend.
GPL frame/bitstream/result structures and eVEncDrvEncode declaration describe caller interfaces, not MMIO programming. No eVEncDrvEncode implementation exists in the examined videocodec C subtree.

public_patch_cross_checks.fact: Author explicitly targets MT8173. The sole h264_write_reg helper is unused; source/BS and SPS/PPS/frame work is delegated through h264_enc_vpu_encode.

Public follow-up removes the unused h264_write_reg helper and documents VPU-writer ownership of working-buffer/shared state. This confirms that its presence in the initial patch was not a direct encoder implementation.
The newer common interface stores input/BS DMA data in shared VSI and calls vpu_enc_encode for SPS/PPS/frame. It still supplies no MT6797 direct-frame registers.

hardware_evidence_boundary.resource_probe: Existing trial35 and later resource observations qualify command-free resource access, clock votes and release only. No encoder frame command, DMA fetch or encoded picture was executed.
hardware_evidence_boundary.idle_reset_probe: Existing idle-reset probe was built but not loaded. Its public pause/reset sequence neither supplies frame setup nor qualifies active-DMA stop or completion IRQ.
hardware_evidence_boundary.same_ip_limit: Matching IRQ/pause/reset offsets across MT6797 and MT8173 does not prove identical source/reference/bitstream/scratch layouts, addressing units, feature controls or revision compatibility.

remaining_implementation_contract: MT6797-compatible source plane addresses, pitch/layout and DMA addressing width/units
Reference/reconstruction surfaces and scratch sizes/layout, with allocation bounds independent of private firmware
Bitstream address/limit units and reliable overflow/error behavior
Picture geometry, fixed-QP/control fields and complete intra-frame start sequence
Completion-source enable, status/result semantics, and active-DMA quiescence before buffer release
SPS/PPS ownership and public H264 output contract, followed by actual encoded-picture validation
mt6797_owner_review_2026_10_11.next_owning_step: Obtain a primary public programming specification or explicit GPL direct encoder implementation with MT6797-compatible IP/revision proof. Then implement one native V4L2 backend using the existing clock/power/SMI ownership, first qualify a bounded fixed-QP intra frame, and retain the full hardware encoder goal. No guessed register writes, private firmware dependency, no-op video node or software encoder substitution is admitted by this source review.
mt6797_owner_review_2026_10_11.excluded_from_new_implementation_inputs: Retained public-hosted PDF extractions carry confidentiality notices; no new facts or bits from them were used here. Confidential verification sources and proprietary codec libraries/firmware were not consulted.
